offers_products.reason: Supplies diabetes, sleep, wound care, urology and ostomy supplies and home medical equipment through Apria and Byram.

offers_services.reason: Delivers home-based care services, respiratory and sleep therapy support, patient education; also rental and servicing of equipment.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Patients at home receive and use the supplies and equipment, such as diabetes and sleep apnea patients.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Connects with insurers and providers who pay and refer; payers like insurers and Medicare are main customers.

recurring_revenue.reason: Ongoing resupply of diabetes, ostomy, urology supplies and monthly equipment rentals like CPAP and oxygen.

cyclical_demand.reason: Medically necessary home care supplies for chronic conditions; patients cannot easily postpone them in a downturn.

big_ticket.reason: Frequent small resupply orders and monthly rentals rather than large infrequent purchases.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue mainly comes from medical supplies and equipment delivered, not primarily clinician time.

large_customers.reason: End buyers are individual patients; payers are large but the patient is the main recipient.

asset_heavy.reason: Needs rental equipment fleets, branches, distribution centers and delivery vehicles for nationwide home care.

notes: Payer-versus-patient buyer mix is inferred; the company was formerly Owens & Minor, and the text suggests the home health business is now the focus.
